newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to pay sex slaves despite S.Korean objection.
newsitem.headline: Japan to pay sex slaves despite S.Korean objection.

text.p: Japan will continue privately paying compensation for Korean women forced to work as sex slaves by Japanese soldiers during World War Two despite Seoul's objections, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"We take it that the project was launched in order to respond to the feelings of aged former comfort women as soon as possible," Kaoru Yosano, deputy chief cabinet secretary, told a news conference.
"Thinking of the current conditions of the former comfort women, we cannot but respect the stand of the fund," he said, using the euphemism Japan adopts to describe the sex slaves.
On Wednesday, South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha was quoted as saying Seoul wanted an immediate halt to the payments.
Last Saturday the Asian Women's Fund, a private group set up in 1995 with heavy Japanese government prodding, paid five million yen ($42,700) to each of seven Korean women.
The fund was initiated by the Japanese government in July 1995 and has pooled donations from Japanese businesses and individuals.

Seoul has eschewed asking for government-to-government compensation for the comfort women, but has said the Japanese government should pay compensation and apologise to the 162 South Korean women officially registered as former sex slaves.
Historians estimate that some 200,000 women from Korea and other Japanese- occupied territories in Asia were forced into sexual slavery for Japanese soldiers before and during the war.

South Korean President Kim Young-sam is to visit Japan on January 25 and 26. He and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto are expected to discuss the issue of cooperation on North Korea, co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup soccer tournament and trade and investment ties.
